title: Ethical Risk and Support for National AI Governance in Bangladesh
content: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) presents potential privacy, bias, misinformation and safety concerns alongside opportunities for innovation. This study examines how stated concern about these risks coexists with support for a national framework for responsible AI governance in 385 adult, AI-aware survey records from Bangladesh. The mixed sample includes law students, graduates, legal professionals and other respondents; it is not presented as representative of the national population. The analysis separates a direct concern statement from statements about safeguards, risk differentiation, rights protection and the national framework. Individual items are examined using response distributions, joint endorsement, paired comparisons and exploratory rank correlations. Overall, 285 respondents (74.0%) endorsed concern about the specified AI risks and 294 (76.4%) endorsed a clear national framework. A total of 228 (59.2%) endorsed both, 57 endorsed concern without framework support, and 66 endorsed framework support without concern. These categories include different response patterns rather than fixed respondent types. The ordinal correlation between the concern and framework items was small; the analysis cannot identify whether risk causes regulatory support. Among 133 recorded law students, results are presented separately as a descriptive subgroup. The paper argues that perceived risks, support for proportionate safeguards and preference for a national framework should be measured independently before theorising how they relate. It recommends scenario-based studies of specific AI harms and regulatory options, explicit institutional-trust measures, and documented sampling and fieldwork procedures.
